newsitem.title: USA: PG&E to acquire Valero in $1.5 billion deal.
newsitem.headline: PG&E to acquire Valero in $1.5 billion deal.

text.p: PG&E Corp. said Friday it planned to merge with San Antonio, Texas-based Valero Energy Corp. and acquire its natural gas services business in a deal valued at $1.5 billion.
San Francisco-based PG&E said the acquisition does not include Valero's wholly owned subsidiary, Valero Refining and Marketing Co., which will be spun off prior to the merger.
Valero Natural Gas Co. operates a 7,500-mile natural gas pipeline system that can carry more than 3 billion cubic feet of gas a day and eight natural gas processing plants in Texas.
Its operations include transporting and marketing natural gas and natural gas liquids and marketing of electric power.

"The combination of our two companies is a natural fit," PG&E Chairman Stanley Skinner said in a statement. "We share the same vision of the convergence of gas and electric energy markets and the key attributes that the successful energy company of the future must bring to the marketplace."
Doug Christopher, an analyst at Crowell, Weedon in Los Angeles, said the deal made sense for PG&E, which is "trying to position itself as a national energy services provider."
The utility is "trying to find other revenue sources to replace the regulated electric utility side of the business," he said.
PG&E is the holding company for the Pacific Gas and Electric Co. utility and natural gas pipeline company Pacific Gas Transmission Co.
Christopher said PG&E already has a strong position in the natural gas distribution business and was positioning itself for a stronger role as distributor of energy services.

The acquisition of Valero Natural Gas would mark PG&E's third recent investment in the natural gas industry in Texas. In December, PG&E acquired Energy Source Inc., a Houston-based gas marketing business.
Earlier this week, PG&E finalized the purchase of Teco Pipeline Co., a Corpus Christi, Texas-based company that operates natural gas gathering, processing, transportation and marketing businesses.
Pacific Gas Transmission owns and operates a natural gas pipeline running from Canada to California.

PG&E said the combination of Valero, Teco, and Energy Source would create one of the top 10 gas marketing operations in the United States, with average daily sales volumes of 3.6 billion cubic feet per day in 1996.
The company said the merger was expected to be completed by mid-1997.
Under the terms of the deal, PG&E will acquire Valero for about $1.5 billion, plus adjustments for working capital and other considerations.
PG&E will issue $722.5 million of common stock, in exchange for outstanding shares of Valero common stock, and will assume some debt and other liabilities.

Each Valero shareholder will receive about 0.63 shares of PG&E common stock for each Valero share, based on a PG&E closing price Thursday of $22.75 per share. The value to Valero shareholders is about $14.25 per share of Valero stock.

Valero's shareholders also will receive one share of the spun-off refining and marketing company. The new refining and marketing company will retain the Valero name and will apply to be listed on the New York Stock Exchange.
Both the spin-off of the refining and marketing business and the merger with a subsidiary of PG&E Corp. are expected to be tax-free transactions for Valero shareholders.
Earlier this month, Valero said potential purchasers had been narrowed down to PG&E as well as Enron Corp., Conoco Inc., Cinergy Corp. and Entergy Corp.
